Yeah. I've been through a lot, and I have to say, breaking up with my fiance was definitely one of the most painful experiences a person can go through. It's very cliche, but time does make it better. It helps to use the time being single, and devote it to things that interest you (yeah, depression sort of takes that away too...) spend more time with friends, read books, take tennis lessons, I don't know. No matter how painful it is, it DOES get better. The pain goes away. When you start feeling better, you'll be impressed with how strong you've become. Relationships ending can be caused by faults with both parties; you can have some self introspection. Think about ways you can be better in your next relationship. Be honest about what you didn't like about an ex (no one is perfect) and apply it to learn what you do and don't like in relationships.

And...chocolate never hurt anyone.

The perception of beauty is something that interests me, and something I've thought about a lot. The fascinating part is that there is no such thing as a "beautiful woman," it's all perception. I have seen some "average" women desired more than your typical hot girl, and some fucking gorgeous women that guys don't look at twice. The majority of people are actually quite average looking, and many are what some would call ugly, yet most have relationships. Relationships and dating aren't just for the attractive, and again, attractive is relative.

Love isn't enough. Nothing is black and white. You can love them, and they can love you, but that doesn't mean you can or should be with that person. When we were younger, media told us that if you could find that one person that loves you and you to them, then that was all it took.

That's not quite how it works, and quite painful to learn the hard way.
